intended_object: The standard σ-sesquilinear form on the coordinate space R^ι, h(x,y) = ∑ᵢ xᵢ σ(yᵢ). It is linear in x and σ-semilinear in y, for a ring automorphism σ of a commutative semiring R. This is the form used for Hermitian duals of codes when σ is an involution, e.g. Frobenius on 𝔽_{q²}. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the `sesquilinearForm_apply` lemma.
explanation:
The body is `Matrix.toLinearMapₛₗ₂' R (RingHom.id R) σ 1`. Mathlib defines it through `toLinearMap₂'Aux`, which gives (v, w) ↦ ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ σ₂(w j) • σ₁(v i) • M i j. With M = 1 and σ₁ = id this is ∑ᵢ xᵢ σ(yᵢ), as the library's simp lemma `sesquilinearForm_apply` states. The type `(ι → R) →ₗ[R] (ι → R) →ₛₗ[σ] R` matches the docstring: linear in the first argument and σ-semilinear in the second. When σ is involutive, the form is Hermitian, which `sesquilinearForm_swap` proves.

On generality:
- R is any commutative semiring. Commutativity is needed for the form to be linear in the first argument. ι is any finite type, which is needed for the finite sum.
- σ is a `RingEquiv` rather than an arbitrary ring endomorphism. This is the standard setting in the literature (sesquilinear forms relative to an automorphism, Hermitian forms for involutive automorphisms). The library also uses invertibility: `sesquilinearForm_flip_bijective` uses σ.symm and nondegeneracy uses injectivity. So this is not a meaningful narrowing.

Mathlib has the general matrix-to-sesquilinear-form construction, which this definition specializes to the identity matrix. Mathlib has no dedicated named definition of this standard σ-twisted dot-product form; `Matrix.dotProductBilin` is only bilinear. So the definition is faithful.
